issues.title: Backward integration does not sample the advertised pushforward

failure_location.quote: sampling $Z \sim \nu$ and solving the ODE backward in time with $z$, a realization of $Z$, to obtain $x = \Phi^{-1}(z)$

issues.failure_explanation: The advertised model distribution is Φ_*ν. If Z∼ν, applying Φ generates that distribution, whereas applying Φ^{-1} generates (Φ^{-1})_*ν. Thus the old executable sampling instruction has the wrong integration direction and output map.
issues.overall_effect: The stated sampling procedure produces the inverse pushforward rather than samples from the generative model; the later abstract mathematical use of Φ_*ν is otherwise unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the executable instruction by drawing X from ν, solving the ODE forward from X on [0,1], and returning Φ(X). Backward integration should be described only as a way to evaluate Φ^{-1} on a given endpoint.
issues.why_classification: The old source consistently defines Φ as the map pushing ν to the model distribution, so the repair is short and uniquely determined. Nevertheless, the sentence gives a coherent but incorrect sampling construction and must be mathematically corrected rather than merely decoded as notation. The repair is local and preserves the model and all later results.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: A sample $z$ from $\Phi_*\nu$ is generated by drawing $X \sim \nu$ and solving \eqref{eq:flow_ode} forward in time with $y_0 = X$ to obtain $x = \Phi(X)$

issues.title: Wrong sign in the Liouville density formula
issues.failure_explanation: Along y=Φ(x), Liouville's formula gives log det DΦ(x)=∫div v(Φ_t(x),t)dt, while change of variables gives f_{Φ_*ν}(y)=f_ν(x)/det DΦ(x). The divergence contribution to log f_{Φ_*ν} must therefore have a minus sign, not the printed plus sign.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed density and any likelihood computed literally from it use the inverse Jacobian-volume correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In equation (eq:liouville_log_det), replace the plus sign immediately preceding the divergence integral by a minus sign.
issues.why_classification: Liouville’s formula and the change-of-variables identity stated in the old source uniquely force the negative sign. No proof or dependent formal result uses the positive sign, and the correction changes no mathematical promise or proof architecture.

issues.title: Wrong characteristic in the Liouville density formula

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Accordingly, we abbreviate $\Phi_t := \Phi_{0,t}$ for flows starting at $t_0 = 0$, and denote by $\Phi := \Phi_{0,1}$ the flow map evaluated at final time $t = 1$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper defines Φ_t as the forward flow from time zero. Therefore the trajectory whose time-one endpoint is y is t↦Φ_t(Φ^{-1}(y)). In general t↦Φ_t(y) is a different trajectory and does not end at y at time one, so the old divergence integral is evaluated on the wrong characteristic.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed pushforward density evaluates the Jacobian correction along an unrelated forward trajectory and therefore gives an incorrect likelihood in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In equation (eq:liouville_log_det), replace the characteristic Φ_t(y) by Φ_t(Φ^{-1}(y)).
issues.why_classification: The old source explicitly defines Φ_t as the forward flow from time zero and Φ as its time-one endpoint. Consequently, Φ^{-1}(y) is uniquely forced as the initial point of the trajectory ending at y. This is a direct correction of the displayed argument, with no downstream inference or guarantee requiring alteration.

issues.title: Missing uniform C^k radius for the target class

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The target class $\mathcal{T} \subset \mathcal{M}_1^+([0,1]^d)$ consists of absolutely continuous measures with densities $f_\mu \in C^k([0,1]^d)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem claims approximation and KL constants uniform over all μ in the target class, while the old assumptions establish only f_μ∈C^k and fixed bounds κ≤f_μ≤K. For d=1 with uniform source, the admissible densities f_{μ,N}(x)=1+a sin(2πNx), 0<a<1, have the same positive upper and lower bounds for every N. Their Knothe–Rosenblatt maps satisfy T_N'=1/f_{μ,N}(T_N), so higher derivatives of T_N, and hence of u^{μ,N}/η on interior points, grow with N. Thus the displayed class-uniform C^k bound cannot depend only on d,k,κ,K, and the uniform approximation and PAC constants do not follow.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform C^1 model approximation and KL model-error rate are not established for the stated unrestricted target class, so the later uniform PAC theorem also loses its model-error input.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a fixed constant M<∞ to the target-class assumptions and require sup_{μ∈T} ||f_μ||_{C^k}≤M. Amend the target-field, approximation, KL, and PAC constants and thresholds to depend on M; the approximation rate and the uniform PAC conclusion then remain valid for this bounded-smoothness target class.
issues.why_classification: A uniform C^k radius supplies the missing source-supported control without changing the transport construction, proof architecture, or rates. It is not a minor exceptional-case qualification, however: it excludes natural high-frequency families allowed by the old target class and makes the uniform theorem conditional on a substantive complexity bound. The resulting theorem and affected PAC chain remain recognizably comparable, so the loss is limited rather than major.

issues.title: Omitted displacement term in flow-Jacobian stability
issues.failure_explanation: Writing a=[Φ_t^θ]^{-1}(x) and b=[Φ_t^μ]^{-1}(x), the proof must control Dv^θ(a)−Du^μ(b). The asserted supremum of D(v^θ−u^μ) controls Dv^θ(a)−Du^μ(a), but omits Du^μ(a)−Du^μ(b). That term requires a spatial Lipschitz bound for Du^μ and an inverse-flow displacement estimate. The same omission recurs when two parameterized fields are compared in the sub-Gaussian argument, where a uniform spatial Lipschitz bound for Dv is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The C^1 flow-Jacobian comparison used for the KL model bound and the parameter-Lipschitz likelihood process is incomplete, so the model-error and generalization chain is not established as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Establish an architecture-dependent uniform W^{2,∞} bound for the bounded-parameter ReQU vector fields, use the available C^2 bound for each target field, and prove inverse-flow displacement estimates. In every Jacobian comparison, split evaluations at different points, for example Dv(a)−Du(b)=[Dv(a)−Du(a)]+[Du(a)−Du(b)], and bound the second term by Lip(Du)||a−b||; use the analogous split with Lip(Dv) in parameter and sample comparisons. Propagate the resulting enlarged constants through the KL model bound, sub-Gaussian lemma, Dudley estimate, concentration theorem, and final PAC theorem.
issues.why_classification: The old smoothness assumptions and bounded ReQU parameters support a repair that preserves the method, rates, and conclusions. But completing it requires a new spatial derivative-Lipschitz estimate, flow-displacement arguments, and coordinated revisions throughout the recorded learning chain. This is contained nontrivial proof work rather than a routine local insertion, while neither global reconstruction nor mathematical loss is necessary.

issues.title: Log-determinant sensitivity bound omits inverse-Jacobian conditioning
issues.failure_explanation: For d=1, take positive scalars A=a and B=2a. The displayed bound reduces to |log a−log(2a)|≤2|a−2a|, i.e. log 2≤2a, which is false for sufficiently small a. A bound for determinant differences does not control log-determinant differences uniformly near zero. The flow estimates can supply a positive lower bound, but the proof never inserts its reciprocal into the sensitivity constant.
issues.overall_effect: The KL model bound, the sub-Gaussian likelihood increments, and the bounded-difference constants all use an unsupported log-Jacobian estimate, so their downstream learning guarantees are not proved with the stated constants.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For each relevant inverse-flow Jacobian A, derive the positive lower bound |det A|≥exp(−C_d R) from the applicable C^1 vector-field bound R. Then combine the ordinary determinant perturbation estimate with |log a−log b|≤|a−b|/min(a,b), inserting the resulting conditioning factor in the KL, sub-Gaussian, and bounded-difference constants and absorbing it into the existing architecture-dependent envelopes.
issues.why_classification: The displayed step is an invalid inference and therefore is not a typo. Nevertheless, the old flow bounds routinely provide both upper Jacobian bounds and the missing positive determinant lower bound. Inserting its reciprocal only enlarges constants of the same asymptotic form; it requires no new proof architecture, rate change, quantifier change, or loss of applicability.

issues.title: Sample-dependent quadrature threshold does not prove rectangular PAC control

failure_location.quote: provided also that the number of quadrature points $m \geq m(n^*)$ is sufficiently large.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: it is possible to choose a threshold $m(n)$ for the number of quadrature points

issues.failure_explanation: The quadrature estimate contains the factor exp(√d√q_n Lip_1^Θ(L_n,W_n)), so the proof establishes, for each n, a sufficient budget m≥m(n). Neither the estimate nor any monotonicity argument shows that m(n*) bounds the required budgets for all n>n*. Consequently, the argument supports only a coupled condition m≥m(n), not the theorem's fixed threshold m(ε,δ) valid independently for every larger n.
issues.overall_effect: The main theorem's independent sample-size and quadrature-budget quantifiers are unsupported; the old proof gives only consistency along a coupled growth of m with n.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace each neural-vector-field hypothesis space by its closed subspace satisfying a fixed C^1 bound ||v||_{C^1}≤r, with r chosen above the uniform target-field bound plus the approximation margin. Verify that the approximating fields eventually lie in this subspace and that restricting the class does not worsen the existing entropy or concentration estimates. The resulting uniform Gronwall bound on ||Φ^θ||_{C^1} then permits one quadrature threshold m(ε,δ) valid for every n above the sample threshold.
issues.why_classification: The dependence of the old quadrature estimate on the growing architecture cannot be removed by the stated m(n*) argument. A fixed regularity truncation gives a contained, source-supported repair preserving the rectangular PAC quantifiers, but it modifies the estimator’s hypothesis class and requires nontrivial approximation and empirical-process checks. Thus it exceeds a minor bookkeeping repair without requiring global reconstruction or weakening the advertised guarantee.
